correctness.rationale: Gaussian invariance forces a centered stationary mean by E[D_I]=I-hH. Exact second and fourth moments of every scalar projection force each conditional Gaussian covariance to equal the common covariance. Each coordinate's off-diagonal equation implies HΣ diagonal, symmetry makes this diagonal commute with H and hence scalar on connected precision components. Exact diagonal variance balance yields γ_C and the strict bound hT_C/P_C<2. The proposed law is preserved by every coordinate kernel via its Gaussian conditional regression; synchronous coupling proves unique invariant under strict coordinatewise stability, and the non-Gaussian complement. This proves all dimensions and boundaries analytically. A standalone exact SymPy checker passed 144 rational covariance and finite-step tests, including a positive fourth-moment mixture discrepancy 192/5929; computations are not substituted for infinite proof.

value.rationale: The Gaussian precision target is the natural calibration problem for the random-coordinate Langevin Euler sampler. The theorem establishes a complete nonlinear property of the invariant probability law (Gaussian versus necessarily non-Gaussian), not merely a stationary covariance or routine error estimate, and gives an exact numerical temperature/KL/Wasserstein calibration for the source's preferred diagonal probabilities. On connected graphs those weights are necessary as well as sufficient. This explicit componentwise boundary is motivated by choosing probabilities for structured quadratic targets and does not pretend to optimize runtime or solve nonlinear sampling.
